summary:
Bali offers the closest approximation to pockets of refuge in Indonesia: LGBTIQ+ people migrate there to "remake the meaning of home" and find spaces where they feel "valued, accepted and able to be themselves, even if those spaces are hidden and limited." No local enforcement actions, discriminatory bylaws, mass raids, or violence waves have been documented against trans visitors. The island sits outside OutRight's eight-province discriminatory-regulation set. However, the 2026 KUHP applies equally: Art. 412 criminalises sex outside marriage and cohabitation (up to one year, complaint-based by spouse/parent/child), and broad "indecency" provisions remain; travel guides advise discretion with public displays of affection for all couples. A 2025 ethnographic study of transpuan communities in Bali explicitly challenges the "romanticised refuge" framing, documenting "resistance and misrecognition" and systemic discrimination even there.

The deviation above the national score reflects absent local enforcement rather than a legal exemption. Materially safer than Jakarta (0.12) with its hotel raids and discriminatory regs, but not a protected space; the new KUHP and Perpres 111/2025 create fresh exposure that could be activated in any police contact.

Berghahn journal article (Anthropology & Medicine, 2025), an ethnographic study of transpuan (trans woman) communities in Bali: deliberately challenges the romanticised "refuge" framing, documenting persistent resistance and misrecognition and systemic discrimination on the island.

LGBTQ+ travel guide for Bali: flags same-sex relations criminalised under the new national penal code with "Exercise Significant Caution" advisory; frames the island as asking couples to keep affection quieter; notes Seminyak, Canggu, Ubud as the consistently gay-friendly areas.

March 2026 travel guide: "Bali is broadly welcoming to LGBTQ+ travellers... 'live and let live'" but the 2026 KUHP adds nuance; same-sex marriage not recognised; public displays of affection discouraged for all couples under conservative norms; no criminal enforcement recorded against tourists.

outOfScopeNotes: Bali's general tourism-hazard profile (traffic, surf, scams) is unrelated to trans risk; the island's relative safety is a social-fact, not a legal exemption.
tangentialFactors: Same-sex conduct provisions (KUHP Art. 412 cohabitation/sex outside marriage) reach trans visitors in couples or shared accommodation, complaint-based but newly available as a leverage tool in any police contact.
